subject: HealthSync deployment ops: scope checklist & evidence requests
messages:
From: Elena Morales <elena.morales@healthsync.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: Samir Rao <samir@medsecure.ai>
Date: Sun, 18 Apr 2027 09:06:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Intro call recap — deployment constraints and security questions

Thanks for the call this morning. A quick recap from HealthSync side: we must keep PHI on customer-controlled VPCs when running inference on-prem for three pilot customers, and any SaaS-hosted solutions require a completed SOC 2 Type II report and evidence of network isolation (subnet diagrams).

Can you share the most up-to-date deployment template and a short checklist of evidence we can pull for procurement? Also, we have a vendor questionnaire (attached) that our InfoSec will send to you formally — Samir from MedSecure will coordinate.

High-level timeline goal: pilot-ready infra in 8–10 weeks, security review completed in 4 weeks.

Best,
Elena
Head of Platform Security | HealthSync

[attachment: vendor_security_questionnaire_healthsync.xlsx (spreadsheet)]

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Morales <elena.morales@healthsync.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 18 Apr 2027 11:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Intro call recap — deployment constraints and security questions

Elena — thanks, great summary. Attaching our deployment template and a short evidence checklist that maps to SOC 2/HIPAA and network isolation items.

A few immediate notes:
- SOC 2: Redwood has a SOC 2 Type II report for our hosted platform; for private/on-prem customers we provide the control mappings and audit logs export process. If HealthSync requires the hosted SOC 2 artifact, we can provide the report under NDA.
- Network isolation: our private deployment supports tenant VPC peering, dedicated subnets, and optional physical air-gap packaging for fully offline pilots. We will need your network diagram (CIDR, transit devices) to confirm compatibility.
- Evidence checklist (attached) includes where to find KMS/HSM config, audit log exports, and retention settings in the Private control plane.

Next steps I propose:
1) I’ll upload the deployment template and questionnaire to a shared Drive folder (link below).
2) Vivek and I will run a quick mapping exercise to HealthSync’s questionnaire and return a redlines/advice doc within 72 business hours.
3) If we need an on-prem air-gapped appliance, we’ll put together scope + hosting requirements and a rough timeline estimate.

Attaching: redwood_deployment_template_v2.pdf; vendor_security_questionnaire_healthsync.xlsx (filled checklist stub).

Jordan Blake
Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
[attachment: redwood_deployment_template_v2.pdf (pdf)]

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 19 Apr 2027 08:17:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: HealthSync deployment ops: scope checklist & evidence requests

Looping in my notes from an initial mapping pass against their attached questionnaire:

- SOC 2: hosted report available; for private deployments we can provide control evidence exports (audit_logs.csv, deploy_audit.pdf) and a SOC-mapping spreadsheet. Need confirmation if legal wants the entire report or just mappings.
- GDPR/HIPAA: data residency for US pilots — HIPAA applies, ensure BAAs for any third-party telemetry or monitoring agents. We must confirm which telemetry endpoints HealthSync is comfortable allowing back to Redwood (metrics vs. payloads).
- Network: ask for explicit diagram showing egress points. If customer requires air-gap, we need: physical rack footprint, power, and console access plan. Air-gap adds ~3–4 week procurement + validation window.
- Identity/KMS: prefer customer-managed KMS (bring-your-own-key). If they choose Redwood KMS, we can document key rotation and HSM provider.

I'll take the questionnaire and draft a redlined answers sheet and a short statement of work (SoW) template to propose on the air-gap option. Jordan — want me to send the redlines directly to Elena or share draft with Lauren first?

— Vivek
Security Engineering | Redwood Inference

From: Elena Morales <elena.morales@healthsync.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: Samir Rao <samir@medsecure.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 11:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: HealthSync deployment ops: scope checklist & evidence requests

Thanks everyone — that plan looks good. A couple quick clarifications:
- For SOC 2, procurement will accept control mappings and evidence for a private deployment; they only request the full report for SaaS vendor contracts.
- HealthSync will prefer customer-managed KMS for pilot 1.
- I'll attach our network diagram and an initial list of pilot site rack specs by EOD Thursday.

Samir (cc): once you push the formal questionnaire over we can label the high-priority sections (network, key mgmt, audit exports).

Next milestones we’ll track:
- 2027-04-22: HealthSync sends network diagram + rack specs
- 2027-04-23: Redwood returns questionnaire redlines and SoW draft
- 2027-04-30: Security review complete (goal)

Thanks,
Elena
Head of Platform Security | HealthSync
